question: Explain when an auditor is required to modify the opinion under SA 705, and how the auditor decides between a qualified opinion, an adverse opinion and a disclaimer of opinion.
sources: SA 705 Modifications to the Opinion in the Independent Auditor's Report

points.label: When the opinion is modified
points.description: The opinion is modified when the auditor concludes, on the evidence obtained, that the financial statements as a whole are not free from material misstatement, or is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence to conclude that they are.
keywords: unable to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence
points.basis: SA 705, circumstances when a modification to the auditor's opinion is required

points.label: Qualified opinion
points.description: Given when misstatements are material but not pervasive, or when the auditor cannot obtain sufficient appropriate evidence and the possible effects of undetected misstatements could be material but not pervasive.

points.label: Adverse opinion
points.description: Given when, having obtained sufficient appropriate evidence, the auditor concludes that misstatements are both material and pervasive.

points.label: Disclaimer of opinion
points.description: Given when the auditor cannot obtain sufficient appropriate evidence and the possible effects of undetected misstatements could be both material and pervasive; also in rare cases with multiple uncertainties whose combined effect makes forming an opinion impossible.

points.label: Meaning of pervasive and the basis section
points.description: Effects are pervasive if they are not confined to specific items, or if confined they form a substantial part of the financial statements, or relate to disclosures fundamental to users' understanding. The report includes a 'Basis for' section describing the matter and, where practicable, quantifying its financial effect.
points.basis: SA 705, definition of pervasive and form and content of the auditor's report when the opinion is modified
